summary: Admin/Moderation Dashboard rebuild + new policy verified end-to-end via 18 pytest cases — ALL 18 PASS (100%). Verified: GET /api/admin/policy returns flag_threshold=3, restrict_threshold=5, window_days=30, auto_ban=false plus 4 rule strings (including 'never auto-banned'); GET /api/admin/summary includes new 'flagged' count under users plus full policy object and 403s for non-admins; GET /api/admin/repeat-offenders returns required shape (user_id, username, first_name, avatar, unique_reporters, total_reports, last_reported_at, reasons[], restricted/flagged_for_review/banned) sorted desc by unique_reporters and 403s for non-admins; threshold logic works as specified — 3 unique reports → flagged_for_review=True with restricted=False AND notices NOT auto-hidden, 4th report still does not restrict, 5th report → restricted=True with restricted_reason mentioning '5', notices auto_hidden=True, admins notified via moderation_urgent notification; CRITICALLY confirmed user.banned remains False even after 10 unique reports — no auto-ban EVER; legacy 24-hour rule is GONE — 3 rapid reports flag but do NOT restrict (auto_restricted=False on all 3 POSTs); POST /api/admin/users/clear-restriction returns 404 for unknown user, 403 for non-admins, on success unsets restricted+flagged_for_review, un-hides notices ($unset auto_hidden), and writes admin_log entry with admin_id+notes; regressions all green: /admin/reports list+status filter, /admin/reports/{id} detail with reporter+target_user+target_history, /admin/support/tickets, /admin/users/{warn,suspend,ban,restore} full roundtrip with mongo verification, /api/community/today, /api/games/wordsearch/daily, frankie demo-login.
critical_code_review_comments: _apply_moderation_policy correctly uses unique reporter SET (db.reports … addToSet semantics in the python set comprehension), so a single reporter spamming reports does not inflate the count — only DISTINCT reporters trigger thresholds. Confirmed via the 3-report flag + 5-report restrict tests.
Policy endpoint /admin/policy is public (no admin gate) — appropriate since it only exposes house rules, no PII.

clear-restriction uses $unset for restricted/flagged keys (clean: leaves no zombie 'restricted: false' artefacts) and properly un-hides notices via $unset auto_hidden. admin_log entry includes admin_id, target_user_id, action='clear_restriction', notes, created_at.

Edge case worth noting (not a bug): if a 6th+ unique report arrives AFTER an admin clears restriction, the next report submission would re-apply restrict because the guard is 'not target.get("restricted")' — this is correct behaviour (a cleared user can still get re-restricted by fresh reports), but worth highlighting for the dashboard UX.
AUTO_RESTRICT_THRESHOLD legacy alias is retained at module top (line 2692) but is unused inside _apply_moderation_policy — could be removed in a future cleanup, but harmless.
seed_data_creation: Created 11 disposable real-account users via /api/auth/signup with the prefix TEST_modpol_<run-id>_ (1 target + 10 reporters) and 1 disposable user for the warn/suspend/ban/restore roundtrip. ALL disposable users + their reports + notices + admin_log entries are deleted in a module-scoped fixture teardown. The 8 canonical demo accounts (maggie, frankie, joycey, billdo, dot, art, eil, roy) were NEVER mutated — maggie/frankie were only used for demo-login (read-only). Run is fully idempotent and safe to re-run.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Test file: /app/backend/tests/test_moderation_policy.py. XML: /app/test_reports/pytest/moderation_policy_results.xml.
